SRC-358:R003.text: 3. TASK PERF-CLOSE-001 — EVIDENCE-GRADE WALL-TIME PROFILER: Add lightweight, low-overhead instrumentation to the ACTUAL closing path, not only standalone synthetic benchmarks. Trace a unique correlation chain: project -> ticket -> verify cycle -> request -> verification identity -> single-flight operation -> executed evidence record -> citation -> phase transition -> final release/publish decision Record separately: request_wall_s process_launch_count python_bootstrap_wall_s (only if measurable) canonical_state_read_wall_s validation_and_conformance_wall_s lock_wait_wall_s fingerprint_wall_s identity_capture_wall_s evidence_lookup_wall_s single_flight_join_wall_s sandbox_copy_wall_s shard_copy_wall_s test_discovery_wall_s actual_test_execution_wall_s compiler_or_external_child_wall_s (if applicable) cleanup_wall_s receipt_write_wall_s evidence_citation_wall_s phase_transition_wall_s ship_gate_wall_s total_ticket_wall_s Include: source_fingerprint baseline_digest verification_identity_digest jobs suite and selected family selected test count actual executed test count cache_reused single_flight_joined force_fresh_reason gate_invoking_the_run rerun_reason record_path + sha256 raw_status + judged_verdict source_change_generation Measure with monotonic clocks for durations and wall clock only for ordering. Capture real subprocess time where possible. Do not attribute unexplained gaps to Python startup. Export small JSON/JSONL telemetry in existing canonical evidence infrastructure with schema/version and bounded retention. Respect confidentiality of paths, environment and secrets. Add one human-readable critical-path summary to the work's verification report. Prefer recording provenance over enormous logs.

SRC-358:R004.text: 4. TASK PERF-CLOSE-002 — WHY A FULL SUITE RAN: Create ONE canonical verification decision/explanation on the existing evidence path: REUSE_VALID_RECORD JOIN_IDENTICAL_IN_FLIGHT RUN_TARGETED_REQUIRED RUN_CERTIFIED_IMPACT RUN_FULL_REQUIRED BLOCK_STALE_OR_INCOMPATIBLE BLOCK_ORACLE_INCONSISTENCY RECONCILE_UNKNOWN_OUTCOME Every full-family execution must name its trigger: NEW_TESTED_SOURCE_BYTES CHANGED_BASELINE CHANGED_TEST_SELECTION CHANGED_VERIFICATION_CONFIGURATION CHANGED_TOOL_OR_RUNTIME_IDENTITY MANDATORY_FULL_ACCEPTANCE_GATE NO_COMPATIBLE_VERIFIED_RECORD EXPLICIT_AUTHORIZED_FRESH_PROBE PRIOR_INCONSISTENCY_INVESTIGATION REPLAY_UNSAFE / UNKNOWN Do not permit a vague phase label (VERIFY/REVIEW/SHIP), a new LOG checkpoint, a model response or a new ticket ID to count as sufficient cause to rerun the same full family. The recorded decision must be deterministic and replayable from canonical evidence and current applicable policy. A caller may request '--fresh' only with an auditable reason, without bypassing authority and budget rules. If source files are unchanged and compatible PASS is current, prefer cite_evidence/reusable_record to running the family again. Each ticket still needs its own canonical citation inside the applicable VERIFY cycle; never paste PASS text or reuse an unrelated ticket's completion receipt. If the latest compatible result is FAIL, an older PASS must not be resurrected. If two same-fingerprint results conflict, preserve both and classify the oracle inconsistency; do not select whichever is greener.

SRC-358:R005.text: 5. TASK PERF-CLOSE-003 — TIERED VERIFICATION THAT PRESERVES SHIP: Use tiers driven by actual scope and project policy: DEV/LOCAL: new focused red/green control and directly dependent tests. IMPACT: certified static impact subset ONLY if existing planner proves coverage. FULL: exact canonical full family when required by current accepted policy. RELEASE: any additional required integration, conformance, installed parity or release gates. The existing verification_impact.py has a conservative policy: uncertainty -> FULL. Keep it. IMPACT evidence must not masquerade as full-family acceptance. During active editing: - Write the reproducing failing negative control. - Make the minimal fix. - Run focused control and dependent tests. - Do not launch 8,548 tests after every tiny edit. - Finish coherent source changes before immutable full verification. At a mandatory SHIP/acceptance boundary: - Reuse exact compatible verified full evidence if valid and accepted by ship_gate. - Otherwise execute the required full suite ONCE for the stable generation. - Reject stale/uncertain/incompatible evidence. - If the source changes after that run, re-evaluate exact required coverage. No universal rule saying 'full suite only once per day' or 'only once per release' is allowed. Requirements and identity, not time of day, decide validity. No ticket may be marked VERIFIED merely because its focused tests passed if the applicable acceptance contract demands full family.

SRC-358:R006.text: 6. TASK PERF-CLOSE-004 — STABLE COHORT REUSE: Find whether a group of tickets shares ONE immutable final tested source generation. If yes, use the SAME authenticated core-unit evidence record across their separate canonical VERIFY cycles when the existing gate permits it and the evidence covers each ticket's applicable requirements. If ticket A and ticket B modify code sequentially, a test from the intermediate generation must not certify the final one. Group final changes where appropriate, run full once against the final coherent tree, then cite the same immutable record to eligible tickets separately. Do not defer mandatory negative controls or ignore per-ticket regression evidence to force batching. Test cohort cases: - Two tickets, same tested fingerprint/identity: reuse. - Code changes between tickets: invalidate relevant evidence. - Baseline changes: invalidate. - Toolchain changes: invalidate. - Test configuration changes: invalidate. - New relevant test appears: expand coverage. - One ticket red: no improper SHIP. - Interrupted batch: canonical partial progress and exact retry. Do not infer exact scope from filename only. Use existing impact/verification semantics.

SRC-358:R007.text: 7. TASK PERF-CLOSE-005 — RED RESULT / FLAKY TEST POLICY: T-1975's distinct evidence records show the SAME fingerprint producing different judged verdicts. Diagnose this first before using same-generation PASS as final trust evidence for that generation. Investigate: - shard interference under jobs=6; - shared fixtures / temp directories; - test-order dependence; - imported module/global state leakage; - filesystem / process races; - inconsistent copied snapshot or runtime environment; - test retries and raw-status versus baseline-verdict distinctions; - resource starvation and timeout; - unstable tests whose failures are inherited or baseline-expected. On first red: 1. Parse the failing family, test IDs, source fingerprint and oracle evidence. 2. Identify whether the red is introduced, inherited, flaky, environmental or unknown. 3. Reproduce with the smallest faithful focused fixture where possible. 4. Fix the root cause or preserve an explicit blocker. 5. Permit a repeat full run only after a concrete cause/need is recorded (changed source, changed environment/configuration, explicit flake confirmation or mandatory acceptance policy). Do not loop full suites until one happens to pass. Do not quietly expand the baseline red set to make work green. Do not mark a FAIL as a PASS based on absence of a newly introduced failure unless the canonical baseline policy explicitly permits that adjudication and proves its source identity. Protect every compatible record's SHA, source fingerprint, actual config and verdict chronology. Add an oracle-conflict regression for identical identity with divergent outcomes.

SRC-358:R008.text: 8. TASK PERF-CLOSE-006 — COST-AWARE BUDGET, NOT A SAFETY BYPASS: Implement configurable verification latency diagnostics, with sensible initial thresholds: Full family exceeds 10 min: emit DIAGNOSTIC / PROGRESS STATUS with currently running family, elapsed time, reason, cache miss and expected budget consumption if available. Repeated same-generation full family requested: require an explicit machine-readable RERUN_REASON and previous evidence reference. Run exceeds its declared timeout/budget: classify and checkpoint using existing safe watchdog/child-process cleanup. Ten minutes is an alert threshold, NOT permission to cancel mandatory tests, claim a PASS, or ignore a blocked gate. Resource budgets must operate within existing authorization and preserve independent Work. Tests must not steal active desktop focus, user input, or working windows. Prefer isolated subprocesses and disposable work trees. Use the existing single_flight for genuinely identical concurrent requests; prove that the measured subprocess count drops to one. Do not 'optimize' by sharing incompatible or mutable evidence. Do not introduce persistent background activity or a new authority grant merely to improve speed.

SRC-358:R010.text: 10. REQUIRED REGRESSION / ACCEPTANCE MATRIX: R01. Same tree, baseline, config and toolchain: PASS reused; no new test processes. R02. Same fingerprint with newer compatible FAIL: old PASS not reused. R03. Identical fingerprint with conflicting red/green: conflict surfaced and investigated. R04. Different source fingerprint: required evidence invalidated. R05. Different baseline: invalidation. R06. Different test collection/configuration: invalidation. R07. Different Python/toolchain/environment identity: invalidation. R08. Unresolved external verification runtime: replay refused. R09. Two simultaneous exact requests: one actual run, two independent citations. R10. Incompatible simultaneous requests: separate work, no cross-contamination. R11. Evidence record truncated or modified: SHIP refuses. R12. Focused/impact evidence presented as full: SHIP refuses where full required. R13. Certified impact on closed domain: focused path accepted only as allowed. R14. Uncertain dynamic dependency: conservative FULL selection. R15. Micro-edit, then another micro-edit: no repeated mandatory full gate mid-edit unless policy requires it. R16. Frozen final generation at mandatory gate: exact full evidence acquired/cited. R17. Two tickets share same immutable final generation: safe record reuse with independent ticket proof. R18. Two tickets from different source generations: no stale reuse. R19. One full run FAIL, second 'fresh' request unchanged: explicit reason needed; no automatic PASS-hunting. R20. Sharded run differs from serial run: deterministic triage without relaxing oracle. R21. Process crash while test family runs: single-flight recovery, no fake PASS. R22. Process crash after run before citation: recover exact evidence safely. R23. Repeated citation of one record: one physical execution in profiler. R24. Performance telemetry missing/invalid: status UNKNOWN, not invented timings. R25. Existing SHIP negative controls remain red for invalid or stale evidence. R26. No human GUI focus steal during routine tests. R27. External Close-Ticket.ps1 unavailable: owner-specific blocker, no fabricated profile. R28. Historical publication pending: never treated as installed runtime proof. PERFORMANCE PROOF Measure at least: Case A: a representative 1–3 file change with narrow regressions; Case B: two tickets sharing one final immutable generation; Case C: one mandatory full suite against a stable tree; Case D: a red run followed by investigation and legitimate rerun. Report baseline versus optimized: ticket_wall_s full_family_execution_count unique_full_record_count reused_record_count single_flight_join_count focused_test_count full_test_count test_execution_wall_s non-test_overhead_wall_s startup_overhead_wall_s compiler_wall_s if present SHIP_ACCEPTANCE_OUTCOME regression_coverage Never claim total user time saved from a laboratory microbenchmark alone; demonstrate at least one real canonical ticket closing path.

EXECUTION ORDER — AUTONOMOUS SHIFT: WAVE A — ORIENT, DO NOT DUPLICATE - Read current .saipen/STATE, BOARD, LOG and latest source receipts. - If another Work item is active, complete or correctly checkpoint it first. - Check for existing owned tasks on verification economics; append to one rather than creating duplicates. - Ensure canonical authenticated admission before protected implementation. WAVE B — ESTABLISH TRUTH - Instrument real current core-unit requests and evidence records. - Explain T-1975's four physical full runs and the same-fingerprint verdict conflict. - Inspect what the current caller does when a compatible record exists. WAVE C — FIX FAST PATH - Connect preflight eligibility/reuse decision to actual production callers. - Remove avoidable identical work without weakening identity or SHIP gates. - Repair recurring full-suite retry triggers if objectively unnecessary. WAVE D — VERIFICATION ECONOMICS - Use targeted controls during editing, impact only when certified. - Use full at required boundaries; reuse already-verified exact evidence. - Prove concurrent identical work single-flights correctly. WAVE E — NONDETERMINISM - Reproduce/confine same-generation verdict disagreement. - Fix fixture/shard/environment root cause or retain an explicit blocker. WAVE F — LIVE ACCEPTANCE - Verify a canonical real ticket close and a two-ticket cohort. - Record before/after numbers, test counts and acceptance outcomes. - Run focused and applicable final conformance gates. - Preserve any remaining external or host-dependent blockers. Do not stop after creating a new report or adding a test fixture. Follow the implementation through the real caller and the applicable acceptance boundary.

SRC-358:R012.text: 12. STRICT SAFETY AND COMPLETION: - No fake operator grants. - No source/Work mutation outside authorized project scope. - No bypass of VERIFY/REVIEW/SHIP contracts. - No immutable evidence tampering. - No false test PASS or stale cross-generation reuse. - No arbitrary green-based retry strategy. - No model-driven repetition of 8,548 tests solely to increase confidence. - No arbitrary disabling of failing tests or unapproved baseline growth. - No new cache or scheduler framework duplicating existing facilities. - No unattended publishing without required separate approval. - No claiming deployment from LOCAL_DONE. Completion is NOT: - a policy document; - 'impact tests pass' without required full acceptance; - a cache helper with no production caller; - a reduced test count without equivalent required coverage; - an unmeasured claim that ticket closure is faster; - a single green outcome after conflicting same-generation verdicts. Completion IS: - real measured bottleneck; - existing verification reuse used correctly; - no unnecessary full-family rerun for identical compatible evidence; - secure refusal for all incompatible/stale/red receipts; - deterministic recovery and correct per-ticket citations; - measured reduction in real ticket closing time; - no regressions to canonical SHIP, authority or publication policy.
